meta.label: New cars
meta.source: EPA and DOE fueleconomy.gov; NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings; Science Based Targets initiative
meta.attribution: Every new car, SUV, minivan and pickup the EPA rated for model year 2026 or 2027, one row per make, nameplate and powertrain (model year 2026 where it exists), from the EPA and DOE vehicle file on fueleconomy.gov. By powertrain the 395 rows are 188 gasoline, 5 diesel, 48 mild hybrid, 45 hybrid, 29 plug-in hybrid and 80 electric. Hydrogen fuel-cell cars are left out because the file gives no fuel cost for them, and vehicles above 8,500 pounds gross vehicle weight, such as heavy-duty pickups and full-size vans, are not in the file. Running cost is the EPA's yearly fuel or electricity cost for the median configuration, for 15,000 miles with 55 per cent city driving at the fuel prices fueleconomy.gov used (at $4.47 a gallon of regular and 15 cents a kilowatt-hour in this file), scored as a share of the cheapest on this list. For a plug-in hybrid it is fueleconomy.gov's combined electricity and gasoline figure, which assumes the share of miles on electricity the EPA sets for that car; each note also gives its cost on gasoline alone. The cheapest to run on this list is electric, so a gasoline vehicle's running-cost score mostly shows how far it sits from electric running costs. Crash ratings are NHTSA's overall stars, joined only to the model NHTSA names with the same year, make and powertrain, and scored on the lowest-rated tested version; a model NHTSA has not tested is left unscored. NHTSA advises comparing frontal crash ratings only between vehicles within 250 pounds of each other. The maker's climate target is SBTi's record for the company whose EPA manufacturer code certifies the vehicle, matched by LEI; a maker SBTi does not list is left unscored, not marked down. Purchase prices are not in these registers and are not scored.
meta.license: US public data (EPA, DOE, NHTSA); SBTi facts cited with credit under its website terms

criteria.label: Fuel and electricity cost a year

products.name: Acura ADX
products.description: The 2026 Acura ADX runs on gasoline and was rated by the EPA in 2 configurations (small station wagons), at 27 to 28 mpg combined.

economical.note: The EPA estimates $2,950 to $3,050 a year in premium gasoline across its 2 configurations, median $2,950, at 27 to 28 mpg combined. That assumes 15,000 miles a year with 55 per cent city driving at $5.48 a gallon, the price behind the EPA's figures in this file. Scored against the cheapest to run on this list ($600 a year scores 100; twice that scores 50).

safety.note: NHTSA overall rating, in stars out of 5, for each tested 2026 version: ACURA ADX SUV N/A AWD: 5; ACURA ADX SUV N/A FWD: 5. Scored on the lowest (5 stars; front 5, side 5, rollover 4). Versions NHTSA has not tested are not counted.
